_about: Measured camera calibration for the video twin projector. Source: video-projection /ue/projectors (vanishing points, confirmed by reprojection, cm-level). UE left-handed world, centimetres.
_axes: forward/up are unit vectors in UE world space; build the rotation with MakeFromXZ(forward, up). Do not convert through Euler angles.
_distortion: The lens follows a division model: scale = 2/(1+sqrt(1-4*K*r^2)), r in tan units. k1/k2 are a least-squares fit of that curve to the shader's existing 1+k1*r^2+k2*r^4 form; fit error is given per camera in source pixels. Replace with the exact model when the material is next rebuilt.

_exclude_boxes_note: 2026-10-16, asked on site: every planter's plants show as the model, everything else in the workstation area takes the video. The runtime desks, partitions and chairs overlap the planter cabinets in the model, so no box can keep a cabinet without also keeping a desk; the boxes are therefore green_only: inside them only pixels the model draws in plant green stay the model (projection.hlsl), and the cabinets themselves take the video. Boxes are generous (the plants render well past their bounds). Earlier trials (cabinet + plant boxes) kept desk ends and a chair.

17.height_note: Z 4617.4 = floor 4320 + 297.4 cm, the height confirmed by the external check in September. The batch calibration used the scene-wide default of 305 cm, which puts the camera above the 3 m ceiling: the depth capture then sees the ceiling 3.4 cm below it and rejects everything.
17.receiver_note: World-space box that may receive video; everything outside stays as modelled. Y: upper bound -1440 stops just short of the row of planter cabinets at Y -1410, so those cabinets, the pantry bar and wall cabinets and the lounge stay virtual; only the workstation area shows video. Z: lower bound 4315 is just under the floor (4320), so inside the workstation area the floor, desk legs and chairs are all covered by video. An earlier setting of 4355 kept the floor virtual, which removed floor smears but left a hard seam through every desk and chair.
17.receiver_note_edge: 2026-10-14: Y upper bound -1440 -> -1250 so the window-side desk and whoever sits there are not cut in half; X lower bound -100 -> 700 so the far planter row (Y -1410, near camera 24) stays out of 17, which from the far end only smeared it.
17.image_mask_note: 2026-10-16, asked on site: the planter cabinets must not appear in the video. The real cabinets (white, a row of planter holes on top, at the pantry end of each desk row) are cut out of camera 17's own picture (polygons drawn on a camera frame, so no view mapping is involved); there the model shows. The real and the model cabinets are not in the same place, which is why world boxes around the model ones did not hide the real ones.
17.receiver_note_1016: 2026-10-16, asked on site: camera 17's video only on the desk block. The runtime desks (SM_F11, rows at X ~1160/1556/2009/2395, each three desks along Y -1841/-1681/-1521, i.e. Y -1931..-1431) and their chairs (X 997..2559) plus the desk-side planter cabinets at the row ends (Y -1430..-1386). Outside it -- far rows beyond X 1030, the column and wall on the right, the pantry side -- stays the model.

18.receiver_note: Hall floor on the camera's side of the white wall. 24.receiver_note: Workstation strip only, same idea as camera 17. In the level the desk row starts at X about 315..340 and the planter cabinet in front of it occupies X about 200..290, so X min 300 sits between them. The tall cabinets on the right stand at Y about -1000..-1130 (excluded by Y max -1150); the glass wall on the left is at Y -1595. Known mismatch: in the footage the real counter (round holes) sits at X about 324..470 and the real desks start near X 490, roughly 1.5 m further in than the model has them. So the counter's image lands on the near end of the virtual desk. Either the model's furniture is placed differently from reality here, or camera 24's position is off; not resolved.

_height_warning: Only camera 17's height (297.4 cm) was confirmed by an external check. 18/21/23/24 are set to the same 297.4 cm on the assumption that identical domes on the same ceiling hang at the same height. That is an assumption, not a measurement; before it they carried the 305 cm scene default, which was not a measurement either.
_camera_view_note: In a camera view (X) only that camera's own video is shown; the other projections are seen from the wrong place there and only smear. false shows them all. Per camera, receiver_feather_cm (default 12) softens the four sides of its receiver box; 0 = hard edge.
_local_light_note: Point, spot and rect lights cast no shadows (the sun still does). Measured on site, RTX 3080 Ti 1600x900: with them the frame took 40 ms instead of 22 ms and 7720 draw calls instead of 1545, video or not; that was the stutter. true brings them back.
_show_status_note: Top-left status line (camera ids, live/recorded, fusion on/off). Hidden on site at the user's request; true shows it again (useful when checking whether a camera is live).
_enabled_note: 17, 24, 18 are measured against their pictures. 19 is prior-only: it matches the model and covers an area no measured camera covers.
_disabled_note: 21 and 23 are measured but off (model furniture mismatch, see their disabled_reason). 20, 22, 25-30 are prior-only and off; each has a disabled_reason.
_stream_note: 2026-10-15: stream_url is the camera's RTSP sub-stream (Media2, 720x576), read directly by the runtime with FFmpeg (VideoTwinRtspReader). Measured on site: the HLS route (MediaMTX converter + Electra) put the projection 3.6 s behind the camera; read directly it is a few hundred ms. ${OFFICE_CAM_PASSWORD} is filled in from that environment variable at runtime, so the password is never in this file. If no picture arrives within 12 s, or it stops for 3 s, the recording Content/Movies/Camera<id>_Real.mp4 plays until the camera is back (the reader keeps reconnecting every 2 s). To go back to the HLS route put the old http://127.0.0.1:8888/cam<id>/index.m3u8 address back (needs the VideoTwinLive converter running).
_receiver_edges: 2026-10-14 on site: box sides moved onto real dividing lines (wall bases, cabinet faces, aisle edges) seen in each camera picture, so no desk, chair or person is cut in half by a box side.
_start_fullscreen_note: 2026-10-16, asked on site: after start the 3D view switches to windowed fullscreen, as F11 does. false keeps the window the kit opens (-windowed 1600x900).
